text:
Incident Bot: PagerDuty alert triggered: org_rate_spike for org:horizonai — sustained high QPS, 95th latency > 3s, queue depth climbing. Paging on-call @Alex R.

Alex R: I'm on. Seeing a sustained 3x traffic burst from HorizonAI starting ~5m ago. Their streaming sessions are dominating the scheduler (long-context streams).

Maya G: Confirmed: multiple 504s reported by customer endpoints, internal traces show heavy kv-cache churn from long contexts. Impact scope appears limited to horizonai org ID 0x7a3.

Eliot S: Quick plan: apply a targeted per-org rate-limit bump (to preserve availability) but lower streaming concurrency and temporarily disable long-context prefetch for that org. Avoid global changes.

Alex R: Agreed. I'll do a surgical hotfix: increase the org token-rate cap to 600rps for 20 minutes, reduce streaming concurrency to 2 for horizonai, and flip their long-context prefetch flag off. Will monitor metrics and revert or escalate if anything odd.

Alex R: Running admin command now (internal CLI):
```
# admin CLI (internal)
redwood admin org-rate adjust --org horizonai --set-token-rate 600 --set-stream-concurrency 2 --set-flag long_context_prefetch=false --expires 1749999188
```

Incident Bot: admin API responded 200 OK — ruleset horizonai-temp-2024-06-14 applied (id: rule_8f4).

Maya G: Metric check 60s after change: horizonai queue depth -> 28 (was 90), p95 latency -> 360ms (was 3.2s). Error rate at org level dropped from 4.8% to 0.9%.

Eliot S: Nice. Keep an eye on token spend — if they were abusing conversational loops we may see cost spike. Also verify KV cache hit rate stabilizes.

Alex R: KV cache hit rate improved from 42% -> 78% post-change; streaming token rate per session decreased. No obvious side-effects on other orgs.

CSM Bot: Notifying customer success: sending pre-canned message to HorizonAI CSM team about temporary mitigation and ETA for follow-up.

Alex R: I'm annotating the incident with the commands run and rule id. Creating a short runbook snippet for handoff: 1) monitor org queue and p95 2) if queue rises again, scoping option: route horizonai to dedicated fallback pool (if available).

Samir K: I'll take next 30m of monitoring. @Alex R handoff?

Alex R: Handoff to Samir K: full context attached above. My notes: rule_id rule_8f4, expires 1749999188, revert with:
```
redwood admin org-rate revert --rule rule_8f4
```
Also contact CSM if customer reports degraded functionality.

Samir K: Got it. I have dashboard links and a Grafana panel pinned. I'll watch and escalate if p95 > 1s for 2 consecutive minutes.

Maya G: After 10m the inbound QPS has normalized to ~1.1x baseline. No new 5xx spikes. Recommend keeping the temporary rule for full 20m window then evaluate.

Eliot S: Post-mortem items to create: 1) investigate why HorizonAI streaming sessions caused cache churn 2) consider per-org streaming defaults 3) automations for targeted RL adjustments.

Samir K: Noted. I'll create the follow-up tickets and include runbook snippets.

Incident Bot: Reminder scheduled: rule rule_8f4 will auto-expire at 1749999188 (in ~5m).

Samir K: 2m until expiry — metrics still green. Rolling the rule revert manually at T+20 to confirm graceful recovery.

Alex R: Thanks for the handoff. Filing a customer-impact note for CSM: "HorizonAI experienced elevated latency and errors; temporary per-org throttling applied to restore availability; no data exposure; investigating workload pattern and will propose config changes."

CSM Bot: Message queued to CSM Slack and email with incident summary and expected follow-up.

Incident Bot: Manual revert executed by Samir K: revert rule rule_8f4 -> 200 OK.

Samir K: Post-revert check: queue depth stable at 30, p95 at 380ms, error rate steady at 1.1%. No regression observed in first 3m post-revert.

Maya G: Marking incident as mitigated. Creating postmortem draft and assigning to eng-ml and infra teams for root-cause analysis (ticket INFRA-5321, ML-1182).

Alex R: Good work team. Quick notes for postmortem: include timeline, commands applied, metrics pre/post, customer comms, and recommended long-term fixes (dedicated pool, streaming-concurrency guardrails, adaptive per-org RL automation). :thumbsup:

Samir K: Taking final ownership of the doc. Closing monitoring window; will reopen if any signals reappear.

Incident Bot: Incident thread closed by Samir K.
